gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Goal Zero Sherpa 100AC's AC outlet is a modified-sine inverter rated 100 W max (US version 110 V/60 Hz; a separate international version runs 220 V/50 Hz). It is also below the 150 W continuous rating ResMed sets as the minimum for an inverter running a newer CPAP, so CPAP users should plug into a DC converter, not the AC outlet.
standout_why: I compared geekchamp, rottenwifi and macmyths (all cited by ChatGPT), Engadget (cited) and thunderboltlaptop. Geekchamp, rottenwifi and macmyths each say they could not establish the Sherpa's continuous AC wattage. None of them gives its waveform. Engadget names only 'one AC port' and gives no rating or waveform. Thunderboltlaptop covers only Amazon no-name banks and never mentions waveform or CPAP. Geekchamp and macmyths give generic advice ('look for pure sine for CPAP') but no maker inverter rating to check a unit against. ChatGPT's own answer told shoppers to look for pure sine and then recommended the Sherpa, which is modified sine. None of these pages says which USB-C port gives 100 W or what recharging accessories the Sherpa takes.
decides: The Sherpa 100AC stays the flight-legal pick for laptops and camera chargers. The page should say its outlet is 100 W modified sine, and that 100 W comes from only one of its two USB-C ports. For the CPAP sub-question ChatGPT keeps asking, both small AC banks (Sherpa 100AC and Omni 20+, each 100 W max and modified sine according to Goal Zero's manual and Omnicharge's FAQ) fall below ResMed's 150 W continuous minimum. Send CPAP users to a ResMed DC converter or a station of 150 W or more. The Omni 20+ needs a menu step (120 V AC mode, not 150 V HVDC) before the outlet works. Its adjustable 5–25 V DC barrel port, up to 100 W, can charge a laptop without the AC conversion step. Our mophie row still reads 'Not checked'. mophie's own US store has no Powerstation Pro AC listing to source it from, so that row should be dropped or sourced from a reviewer.

findings.label: AC outlet rating and waveform (US version)
findings.value: 110 V, up to 0.9 A, 100 W max, 60 Hz, modified sine wave (no surge rating listed)
findings.source_title: GOAL ZERO SHERPA 100AC user guide, page 5: FAQ and Technical Specifications (ManualsLib)
findings.note: ManualsLib copy of Goal Zero's own user guide. I also opened Goal Zero's PDF at cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0551/1806/9863/files/Sherpa_100AC_User_guide.pdf, but its text could not be extracted, and goalzero.com returned HTTP 429.

findings.label: International version AC outlet
findings.value: 220 V, up to 0.45 A, 100 W max, 50 Hz, modified sine wave
findings.source_title: GOAL ZERO SHERPA 100AC user guide, page 5: Technical Specifications (ManualsLib)
findings.note: The manual lists separate US and international inverter versions, so a US unit outputs 110 V/60 Hz only. Same mirror caveat as above.

findings.label: USB-C ports (which one gives 100 W)
findings.value: USB-C PD 1: 60 W in and out. USB-C PD 2: 60 W in, 100 W out (5–20 V up to 5 A). The FAQ says the cable and the device must both be 100 W-capable.
findings.source_title: GOAL ZERO SHERPA 100AC user guide, page 5 (ManualsLib)
findings.note: Conflict: the goalzero.com store listing 'New Sherpa 100AC' (read 2026-11-14 via storecheck search) says 'Two High-Speed Power Delivery Ports At 60 Watts each'. The manual's 100 W figure applies to port 2 only.

findings.label: Solar input and paired panels
findings.value: 8 mm solar input 14–22 V, 60 W max. Manual charge times: Nomad 50 4–8 h, Nomad 20 8–16 h, 60 W USB-C source 2 h.
findings.source_title: GOAL ZERO SHERPA 100AC user guide, page 5 (ManualsLib)
findings.note: Goal Zero's Nomad 20 store page (https://www.goalzero.com/products/nomad-20-solar-panel, read 2026-11-14) gives 7.5–15 h for the Sherpa 100AC instead of the manual's 8–16 h.

findings.label: Wall/car recharge accessories (sold separately)
findings.value: Recharges from AC or 12 V through the 8 mm port, using the 12 V car charging cable or the Sherpa Power Supply (both sold separately), or from a 65 W USB-C charger (about 2 h). The guide recommends the Nomad 50 for solar.
findings.source_title: Charge Before Use; Using The Sherpa - GOAL ZERO SHERPA 100AC (ManualsLib page 4)
findings.note: Pass-through is supported, but if output exceeds input the battery drains and the unit turns off.

findings.label: Price at the maker's US store
findings.note: From storecheck.py search of goalzero.com, listed as available. The product endpoint returned HTTP 429.

findings.label: AC outlet mode and waveform
findings.value: You must select 120 V AC mode (instead of 150 V HVDC) in the menu by double-pressing the power button. Omnicharge states the AC output is modified sine wave.
findings.note: The FAQ index shows only truncated previews. The AC wattage (100 W) is on our existing row but was not re-read on an Omnicharge page today, because omnicharge.co returned HTTP 429.

findings.label: DC barrel and USB-C limits for laptops
findings.value: DC barrel: 5–25 V, up to 5 A, 100 W max, must be enabled in the menu. USB-C: 60 W max, available only on the latest Omni 20+. USB-A: 18 W max. Capacity 71 Wh, allowed in carry-on.
findings.note: The FAQ says the laptop must fall within the 100 W (5–25 V, up to 5 A) DC limit.

findings.label: Price at the maker's US store
findings.note: storecheck.py search of omnicharge.co, SKU OP2HA004, listed as available.

findings.label: ResMed minimum inverter rating for running a CPAP from AC
findings.value: Newer machines: a modified sine wave inverter with a continuous rating of 150 W or higher. Older machines with H2i/H3i/H4i humidifiers: pure sine, 300 W continuous, 500 W peak/surge. ResMed DC converters are offered for AirMini, AirSense 10, AirCurve 10, Lumis and S9.
findings.source_title: I am going camping. What do I need to run my sleep apnea machine? – ResMed Australia
findings.note: Arithmetic: Sherpa 100AC (100 W max) and Omni 20+ (100 W) are below ResMed's 150 W minimum. This is ResMed's Australian page with no date (footer © 2026), and it does not name the AirSense 11.

findings.label: AC output, capacity and price at the maker's US store
findings.value: 128 Wh LiFePO4, one AC outlet at 200 W, 10 ms UPS mode, solar input 'PV60'. Price $119.
findings.note: From storecheck.py product. At 200 W the AC outlet clears ResMed's 150 W minimum. The page text does not state the waveform.
